responseItems.question: If a March order vacates only one of two units from a castle area, leaving one unit behind, does the player keep control of that castle area without placing a power token?
responseItems.answer:
Yes. A land area is controlled while you have at least one Footman, Knight, or Siege Engine in it; you only “vacate” an area when **no unit is left behind**. Since one unit remains, the area is not vacated, so you retain control without placing a Power token.

- “Resolve March Orders” says a player vacates an area only when he “leaves no unit behind” (rules, p. 15).
- “Controlling Areas” says a House controls a land area when it has at least one Footman, Knight, or Siege Engine in the area, or has previously established control with a Power token (rules, p. 24).
- Establishing control by placing a Power token is only needed when you vacate the land area with all your units during a March Order (rules, p. 24).

So no Power token is required in the situation described.

actionOutputSchema.title: resolve_march_args
actionOutputSchema.description: You are resolving one of your March orders. Choose which units move and their destinations. Units you omit remain in the source area; you may split an army across destinations, and a single unit can march on its own. An empty moves list removes this March order without moving anyone. Only one destination may start combat. Use the reachable destinations in actionGuidance and keep the resulting armies within Supply. Leaving a control token costs one available power token and preserves control of the source when you legally vacate it. Compare castles gained and lost, and count support around the destination battlefield before choosing an attack. Before attacking another army, use check_neighbours on that battlefield to verify the supporting areas. Your final answer resolves this one order; another remaining order is a later decision.
